bilingual.notes: SBEC issues a Bilingual Education Supplemental certificate (19 TAC §233.6); a new Core/Bilingual Education Spanish with the Science of Teaching Reading: EC-Grade 6 base certificate becomes issuable Sept 1, 2028 (§233.2(f)). Required exams include the Bilingual Target Language Proficiency Test (BTLPT, #190), the Bilingual Supplemental (#164), Core Subjects EC-6 (or grade-band equivalent), and PPR or edTPA. Texas also recognizes a Bilingual Special Education Supplemental EC-12 effective Sept 1, 2027 (§233.8(a)). Practicum (clinical) experience left null as a separate flag because the EPP route bundles it; will revisit when the schema separates EPP-embedded vs. standalone practicum.

eld.notes: SBEC issues an English as a Second Language Supplemental certificate (19 TAC §233.7), required for any teacher serving emergent bilingual students in an ESL program (TEC §29.061). A Core/ESL Supplemental with the Science of Teaching Reading: EC-Grade 6 base certificate becomes issuable Sept 1, 2028 (§233.2(g)). Required exam: ESL Supplemental (#154) plus PPR or edTPA. No target-language proficiency exam is required for ESL.

sei.notes: Texas mandates bilingual or ESL services for emergent bilingual students (TEC Chapter 29 Subchapter B; 19 TAC §§89.1201, 89.1205, 89.1210), but those services are delivered by appropriately certified bilingual or ESL teachers — Texas does not impose an SEI training requirement on all classroom teachers.

history.title: Texas Bilingual Education and Training Act enacted (SB 121, 63rd Legislature)
history.description: Texas became the third state (after Massachusetts 1971 and New Mexico 1973) to mandate bilingual education by statute. SB 121 required school districts with 20 or more EL students of the same language background in the same grade level (K-3) to provide bilingual instruction, and authorized the Texas Education Agency to certify bilingual teachers. The law was substantially expanded by SB 477 (1981) — passed in the wake of the U.S. v. Texas (Civ. Action 5281) federal-court order — to cover K-elementary and to require both bilingual and ESL programs depending on enrollment thresholds. The current 19 TAC Chapter 89 framework descends from this statutory backbone.

history.title: Castañeda v. Pickard decided by the Fifth Circuit (648 F.2d 989)
history.description: Arising out of the Raymondville, Texas ISD, the Fifth Circuit established the three-prong test that federal courts use to evaluate state and district compliance with the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974: (1) the program must be based on sound educational theory; (2) it must be implemented effectively with adequate resources and personnel; and (3) the district must evaluate the program and modify it if it is not producing results. The Castañeda standard remains the controlling EEOA test for EL programs nationwide and is the doctrinal anchor cited in the 2011 DOJ settlement with Massachusetts and the Flores v. Arizona litigation.
